verses.text: Two days later, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.
Jesus and his disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They’re out of wine.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, why bring this to me? My time hasn’t come yet.”
His mother told the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
There were six stone water jars there, used for Jewish purification rituals. Each held about twenty or thirty gallons.
Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them all the way to the top.
Then he said, “Now scoop some out and take it to the head of the banquet.” They did.
The head of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine. He didn’t know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. He called the bridegroom over
and said, “Everyone serves the best wine first. After the guests have had plenty, they serve the cheaper wine. But you’ve saved the best wine until now!”
Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this, he went down to Capernaum with his mother, brothers, and disciples. They stayed there a few days.
The Jewish Passover was coming soon, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers sitting at their tables.
He made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple courts, including the sheep and cattle. He scattered the money changers’ coins and flipped over their tables.
He told the people selling doves, “Get these out of here! Don’t turn my Father’s house into a marketplace!”
His disciples remembered what Scripture says: “Passion for your house will consume me.”
The Jews responded, “What sign can you show us to prove you have the right to do this?”
Jesus answered, “Tear down this temple, and I’ll raise it up in three days.”
The Jews said, “This temple took forty-six years to build. You’re going to raise it up in three days?”
But he was talking about the temple of his body.
After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered he had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and what Jesus had said.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for Passover during the feast, many people believed in his name because they saw the signs he was doing.
But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
He didn’t need anyone to tell him what people were like. He knew what was in every person.
